maya: quick q - following the RFC, are we leaning toward a query-sidecar for RBAC checks or doing inline enforcement in the query executor? perf/complexity tradeoffs incoming
liam: sidecar wins for decoupling & incremental rollout. keeps executor simpler.
nora: sidecar = extra network hop. worried about p50/P99 adding ~1-3ms? depends on colocated vs separate pod.
maya: good callout. if we co-locate sidecar in same pod (unix socket) hop is negligible. but that increases coupling in deployment model.
sam: inline reduces hops and allows batching RBAC checks alongside fetches, better throughput. but it doubles auth logic surface in executors.
liam: another cost: cache invalidation. sidecar can own auth cache w/ central invalidator. inline means each executor must replicate invalidation logic -> more complexity.
nora: also testability. sidecar easier to run unit/integration tests against; we can swap implementations behind API.
maya: perf experiments idea: implement a lightweight sidecar prototype that uses unix socket; measure p50/p99 + cpu. also simulate burst QPS with existing harness.
liam: agreed. propose metrics: added latency, tail latency spike rate, CPU delta on executor, cache hit rate, failure modes (sidecar OOM, RPC timeouts).
nora: don't forget cost model: extra container per node in Dedicated -> resource accounting. include per-request cost estimate.
sam: for rollout: feature-flag sidecar checks per-tenant. start with disabled for enterprise tenants, opt-in for internal staging.
maya: ops/console impact: console route needs to know when RBAC validation fails to render a graceful placeholder vs 500. Add new error codes: AUTHZ_DENIED_VIEW vs AUTHZ_SERVICE_FAIL.
liam: +1. add to SDK docs and console UI mapping.
nora: question on caching keys: should we cache per-user-per-route or per-role-per-route? per-user high cardinality -> mem blowup. recommend per-role + per-tenant.
sam: if we cache per-role we need fast refresh when role membership changes. hook into identity change webhook; sidecar subscribes to kafka topic to invalidate.
maya: rough plan: 1) prototype sidecar unix-socket (2 weeks), 2) bench vs inline minimal impl (1 week), 3) pick direction and write RFC addendum with rollout + failure modes. agree?
liam: +1
nora: +1, I'll sketch invalidation design and eviction policy.
dev-bot: canary deploy started for sidecar-proto -> cluster/staging at maya/1762203333
maya: thanks. we'll sync at next arch sync. tagging @eng-sre for SLO considerations.

Example socket config (proto):
```
# sidecar listen config
socket_path: /var/run/rbac-sidecar.sock
max_conns: 256
cache_ttl_ms: 60000
```

Experiment checklist:
- implement minimal unix-socket sidecar + small auth cache
- bench with console harness: 1k qps steady, 10k qps spike
- collect: p50, p95, p99, cpu/mem, cache hit rate, error rates
- validate graceful UI mapping for AUTHZ_DENIED_VIEW vs 500

Leaving notes here so we don't lose followups.
